title: Indirect Tax Compliance Manager
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI Finance is responsible for ensuring the organization is set up for success in pursuit of its mission.

OpenAI’s Tax and Trade team sits at the center of OpenAI’s global growth—shaping how cutting-edge AI products, partnerships, and infrastructure scale across borders while navigating complex tax, trade, and regulatory regimes. We operate as strategic operators, not just compliance experts, embedding early in product, finance, policy, and infrastructure decisions to manage risk, unlock incentives, and enable OpenAI to grow responsibly and competitively worldwide.

As OpenAI’s products, monetization models, and global infrastructure expand, our tax systems must scale with the same rigor and reliability as our product architecture. The team partners deeply with Financial Engineering, Product Engineering, and Finance Systems to build a modern tax technology stack that enables accurate, real-time tax determination across OpenAI’s global business.

About the Role

We’re hiring an Indirect Tax Compliance Manager to own and continuously improve our end-to-end indirect tax compliance process. This role will be responsible for driving timely, accurate compliance, maintaining audit readiness, and building scalable processes that improve visibility, control, and efficiency across the Tax function. While the role is primarily focused on US indirect tax compliance, the scope may expand over time to support international indirect tax compliance as the team and business continue to grow.

You will sit at the intersection of Tax, Accounting, Finance, and cross-functional business teams, helping ensure that tax compliance is well-controlled, well-documented, and supported by reliable data and technology. The ideal candidate brings strong US indirect tax compliance experience, a detail-oriented and process-driven mindset, and a genuine passion for leveraging technology to streamline and improve compliance operations. A strong interest in automation, analytics, and process improvement are important for success in this role.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA, and we use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week.

In this Role, you will:

  • Own the end-to-end US indirect tax compliance process, including data gathering, return support, filing coordination, payments, reconciliations, and post-filing documentation.

  • Manage day-to-day compliance operations and partner with external service providers to ensure timely, accurate preparation and submission of US indirect tax filings.

  • Develop and maintain audit-ready workpapers, reconciliations, process documentation, and supporting evidence for internal and external audits.

  • Coordinate responses to tax authority notices, audits, and information requests, working closely with internal stakeholders and outside advisors.

  • Strengthen the control environment around tax compliance by designing, documenting, and improving key controls and review procedures.

  • Streamline the end-to-end compliance process by identifying automation opportunities, reducing manual work, and standardizing repeatable workflows.

  • Use tools to build dashboards, monitor compliance status, track KPIs, identify anomalies, and improve reporting visibility.

  • Partner cross-functionally with Accounting, Finance, Legal, and business teams to ensure indirect tax requirements are incorporated into upstream processes and downstream reporting.

  • Review and validate tax data from ERP, billing, and other source systems to support accurate filings and reconciliations.

  • Support new products, process changes, and system implementations by assessing compliance impacts and helping operationalize requirements.

  • Monitor changes in US indirect tax rules, filing requirements, and compliance obligations, and translate them into practical process updates.

  • Build scalable documentation and operational playbooks that make the compliance process easier to manage, review, and improve over time.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • 6+ years of relevant experience in US indirect tax compliance, tax operations, or a related role in industry or public accounting.

  • Strong experience with US indirect tax compliance processes, audit support, reconciliations, and documentation, alongside a strong interest in expanding compliance capabilities to support other jurisdictions.

  • Experience managing or partnering with outsourced compliance providers and coordinating across multiple stakeholders.

  • An enthusiasm for using technology, automation, and analytics to improve tax processes.

  • A strong systems mindset, with experience working across spreadsheets, ERP systems, billing data, and tax-related workflows.

  • Proven ability to identify process gaps, improve controls, and drive operational efficiencies across the compliance lifecycle.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including comfort working with large data sets and transaction-level detail.

  • Excellent communication and project management skills, with the ability to work effectively across Tax, Finance, Accounting and external advisors.

  • High attention to detail, strong organizational skills, and the ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced environment.

  • CPA or advanced degree in Accounting, Tax, Finance, or a related field.

  • Experience in a high-growth or technology-driven environment.

  • Experience with tax engines, ERP platforms and compliance technology tools such as Stripe, Vertex, Oracle, or similar systems.

  • Experience building process reporting, dashboards and workflow visibility tools.

title: Applied Data Science & Machine Learning Leader - Global Forecasting
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Strategic Finance team at OpenAI plays a critical role in shaping the company’s long-term trajectory. We partner closely with Product, Engineering, and Go-to-Market teams to inform high-stakes decisions through rigorous data science and economic modeling.

As part of our expanding Data Science function, we’re building a best-in-class forecasting capability to drive real-time, data-driven decision-making across user growth, revenue, compute infrastructure, and more.

We are developing a scalable forecasting platform to help us understand and anticipate business dynamics in an increasingly complex, usage-based world. Our models are foundational to planning, pricing, operational efficiency, and growth strategy — supporting key investment decisions and unlocking OpenAI’s full potential.

About the Role

We’re looking for a hands-on technical leader to build and lead a small but mighty team of applied data scientists and ML engineers to develop forecasting capabilities and platforms from the ground up.

Your team will be responsible for building and scaling robust, interpretable, and production-ready forecasting systems. These models will power critical business decisions by predicting core metrics such as DAU/WAU, revenue, compute consumption, and profitability.

You will work closely with Strategic Finance leaders to integrate these scalable forecasting capabilities into their operational rhythms and collaborate with the Growth team to forecast key KPIs.

This is a highly cross-functional role that requires technical excellence, strong product intuition, and business acumen. You’ll collaborate with various partners to operationalize forecasting insights, influence company-wide strategy, and build foundational forecasting capabilities at OpenAI.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We follow a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Build and manage a world-class team of applied data scientists and ML engineers to develop forecasting platforms at scale.

  • Design and own the roadmap for the forecasting platform in partnership with cross-functional stakeholders.

  • Collaborate closely with Strategic Finance teams to ensure forecasts are well integrated into planning processes, and executive decision-making.

  • Work closely with cross-functional partners to help them adopt scientific, automated forecasting solutions.

  • Own the end-to-end modeling lifecycle, including scoping, feature engineering, model development and prototyping, experimentation, deployment, monitoring, and explainability.

  • Research and evaluate emerging tools and techniques in the forecasting space.

  • Translate technical outputs into business-aligned recommendations and decision frameworks.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • Extensive experience building production-ready models for time series applications.

  • Proven track record of building adjustable and explainable forecast models for multiple planning cycles.

  • 10+ years of applied data science & engineering experience, with deep hands-on expertise in forecasting and predictive modeling.

  • Demonstrated experience with model monitoring, debugging, and long-term maintenance in production environments.

  • Excellent communication and storytelling skills — able to simplify complexity and influence executive stakeholders.

  • Team leadership experience with a track record of building high-performing, engaged teams.

  • An advanced degree (MS or PhD) in a quantitative field (e.g., Statistics, Computer Science, Economics, Operations Research).

  • A self-directed, intellectually curious mindset and comfort leading ambiguous projects from 0→1.

  • The ability to thrive in a dynamic environment — flexible, resourceful, and willing to do what it takes to succeed.

  • Experience building or scaling forecasting platforms in a high-growth company.

title: Administrative Business Partner (Technical Leadership Support)
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Our Executive Operations team includes Executive Business Partners and Administrative Business Partners, who serve as trusted advisors and collaborators to OpenAIs executives and leaders, focused on strong communication and operational excellence across teams. With a focus on elevating the impact and efficiency of leadership, we anticipate needs, streamline processes, and provide comprehensive support to ensure our executives can focus on high-impact initiatives. We play a pivotal role in driving success and achieving key milestones by cultivating strong relationships and leveraging our deep understanding of business objectives. With a commitment to excellence and a proactive approach, we are dedicated to empowering our leaders and contributing to the overall growth and success of the company.

Our leadership team reflects OpenAI’s culture and core values and is a mission-driven, kind, and thoughtful group. We take pride in creating a work environment that fosters collaboration, open communication, and authenticity, making OpenAI an excellent place to work for highly accomplished professionals.

We’re looking for an Administrative Business Partner to support 2-3 technical leaders within the ChatGPT portfolio.

The ChatGPT team works across research, engineering, product, and design to bring OpenAI’s technology to the world - we learn from deployment and broadly distribute the benefits of AI, while ensuring that this powerful tool is used responsibly and safely. We aim to make our innovative tools globally accessible, transcending geographic, economic, or platform barriers. Our commitment is to facilitate the use of AI to enhance lives, fostered by rigorous insights into how people use our product. 

About the Role: 

The Administrative Business Partner will be a proactive and adaptable partner to leaders who will support complex calendar / schedule management, handle expenses, organize team meetings such as All-Hands, offsites, happy hours, etc as well as arrange travel when needed. This role demands a high-level of coordination for both internal and external engagements, working closely under the guidance of our Executive Business Partners.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Efficiently manage and organize calendars for multiple leaders, ensuring an optimal schedule that accommodates internal and external commitments

  • Take charge of coordinating internal meetings, including scheduling, forecasting, and resolving scheduling conflicts

  • Plan and organize comprehensive travel itineraries, ensuring smooth and efficient travel experiences for leaders

  • Assist in the planning and execution of team offsites, all-hands, happy hours, etc. contributing to team building and strategic planning initiatives

  • Work closely with the broader executive operations team, facilitating effective communication and collaboration within the team and with external partners

  • Process and manage expense reports, ensuring timely submission and adherence to company policies

You might thrive in this role if you have / are:

  • 4-6 years of administrative experience

  • Worked directly with technical teams (Engineering, Product, Design, Data Science, TPM) in a high-growth startup, or similar environment

  • Proven track record of scheduling (often complex & urgent) internal and external meetings and quickly resolving conflicts

  • Experience in managing travel arrangements, including flight / transportation, lodging and entertainment

  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills

  • Extreme fluency in Slack, Google Calendar, Docs, Sheets, Gmail, etc. and other modern productivity technology, and are excited to learn and use new tools

  • One-team mindset - partnership and collaboration is a cornerstone in how you operate

  • Extreme attention to detail - it’s not a personality trait but an exercised functional skill

  • Capable and comfortable working in a rapidly changing and often ambiguous environment

title: Data Scientist, User Operations
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s User Operations organization is building the data and intelligence layer behind AI-assisted operations — the systems that decide when automation should help users, when humans should step in, and how both improve over time. Our flagship platform is transforming customer support into a model for “agent-first” operations across OpenAI.

About the Role

As a Data Scientist on User Operations, you’ll design the models, metrics, and experimentation frameworks that power OpenAI’s human-AI collaboration loop. You’ll build systems that measure quality, optimize automation, and turn operational data into insights that improve product and user experience at scale. You’ll partner closely with Support Automation Engineering, Product, and Data Engineering to ensure our data systems are production-grade, trusted, and impactful.

This role is based in San Francisco or New York City. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

Why it matters

Every conversation users have with OpenAI products produces signals about how humans and AI interact. User Ops Data Science turns those signals into insights that shape how we support users today and design agentic systems for tomorrow. This is a unique opportunity to help define how AI collaboration at scale is measured and improved inside OpenAI.

In this role, you will:

  • Build and own metrics, classifiers, and data pipelines that determine automation eligibility, effectiveness, and guardrails.

  • Design and evaluate experiments that quantify the impact of automation and AI systems on user outcomes like resolution quality and satisfaction.

  • Develop predictive and statistical models that improve how OpenAI’s support systems automate, measure, and learn from user interactions.

  • Partner with engineering and product teams to create feedback loops that continuously improve our AI agents and knowledge systems.

  • Translate complex data into clear, actionable insights for leadership and cross-functional stakeholders.

  • Develop and socialize dashboards, applications, and other ways of enabling the team and company to answer product data questions in a self-serve way

  • Contribute to establishing data science standards and best practices in an AI-native operations environment.

  • Partner with other data scientists across the company to share knowledge and continually synthesize learnings across the organization

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • 10+ years of experience in data science roles within product or technology organizations.

  • Expertise in statistics and causal inference, applied in both experimentation and observational causal inference studies.

  • Expert-level SQL and proficiency in Python for analytics, modeling, and experimentation.

  • Proven experience designing and interpreting experiments and making statistically sound recommendations.

  • Experience building data systems or pipelines that power production workflows or ML-based decisioning.

  • Experience developing and extracting insights from business intelligence tools, such as Mode, Tableau, and Looker.

  • Strategic and impact-driven mindset, capable of translating complex business problems into actionable frameworks.

  • Ability to build relationships with diverse stakeholders and cultivate strong partnerships.

  • Strong communication skills, including the ability to bridge technical and non-technical stakeholders and collaborate across various functions to ensure business impact.

  • Ability to operate effectively in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment with limited structure.

  • Strong communication skills and the ability to translate complex data into stories for non-technical partners.

Nice-to-haves:

  • Familiarity with large language models or AI-assisted operations platforms.

  • Experience in operational automation or customer support analytics.

  • Background in experimentation infrastructure or human-AI interaction systems.

descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Strategic Finance team at OpenAI plays a critical role in shaping the company’s long-term trajectory. We partner closely with Product, Engineering, and Go-to-Market teams to inform high-stakes decisions through rigorous data science and economic modeling.

As part of our expanding Data Science function, we’re building a best-in-class forecasting capability to drive real-time, data-driven decision-making across user growth, revenue, compute infrastructure, and more.

We are developing a scalable forecasting platform to help us understand and anticipate business dynamics in an increasingly complex, usage-based world. Our models are foundational to planning, pricing, operational efficiency, and growth strategy — supporting key investment decisions and unlocking OpenAI’s full potential.

About the Role

We’re looking for a hands-on technical leader to build and lead a small but mighty team of applied data scientists and ML engineers to develop forecasting capabilities and platforms from the ground up.

Your team will be responsible for building and scaling robust, interpretable, and production-ready forecasting systems. These models will power critical business decisions by predicting core metrics such as DAU/WAU, revenue, compute consumption, and profitability.

You will work closely with Strategic Finance leaders to integrate these scalable forecasting capabilities into their operational rhythms and collaborate with the Growth team to forecast key KPIs.

This is a highly cross-functional role that requires technical excellence, strong product intuition, and business acumen. You’ll collaborate with various partners to operationalize forecasting insights, influence company-wide strategy, and build foundational forecasting capabilities at OpenAI.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We follow a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Build and manage a world-class team of applied data scientists and ML engineers to develop forecasting platforms at scale.

  • Design and own the roadmap for the forecasting platform in partnership with cross-functional stakeholders.

  • Collaborate closely with Strategic Finance teams to ensure forecasts are well integrated into planning processes, and executive decision-making.

  • Work closely with cross-functional partners to help them adopt scientific, automated forecasting solutions.

  • Own the end-to-end modeling lifecycle, including scoping, feature engineering, model development and prototyping, experimentation, deployment, monitoring, and explainability.

  • Research and evaluate emerging tools and techniques in the forecasting space.

  • Translate technical outputs into business-aligned recommendations and decision frameworks.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • Extensive experience building production-ready models for time series applications.

  • Proven track record of building adjustable and explainable forecast models for multiple planning cycles.

  • 10+ years of applied data science & engineering experience, with deep hands-on expertise in forecasting and predictive modeling.

  • Demonstrated experience with model monitoring, debugging, and long-term maintenance in production environments.

  • Excellent communication and storytelling skills — able to simplify complexity and influence executive stakeholders.

  • Team leadership experience with a track record of building high-performing, engaged teams.

  • An advanced degree (MS or PhD) in a quantitative field (e.g., Statistics, Computer Science, Economics, Operations Research).

  • A self-directed, intellectually curious mindset and comfort leading ambiguous projects from 0→1.

  • The ability to thrive in a dynamic environment — flexible, resourceful, and willing to do what it takes to succeed.

Bonus if you have:

  • Experience building or scaling forecasting platforms in a high-growth company.

  • A passion for AI and a strong perspective on how machine learning should inform strategic decisions in fast-moving environments.

title: Site Operations Lead
descriptionHtml:
About Team

Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and advancing toward AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world environments. Working across the full model and systems stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the physical constraints of real-world systems to improve people’s lives.

About the Role

As the Site Operations Lead for Robotics, you will own the build-out and day-to-day execution of a production-like facility that enables robotics development, testing, and manufacturing work. This role is responsible for getting the site stood up and running smoothly: coordinating activities during construction and ramp, establishing the operating system for the space, and ensuring daily execution across manufacturing lines, warehousing, internal material movement, and overall site readiness.

This is an on-the-ground leadership role with high ownership of execution, safety, and site reliability. The Site Operations Lead partners closely with Facilities, Safety, Engineering, and Operations teams, and coordinates contractor teams to keep work moving at speed with strong operational control.

This role is based in the San Francisco Bay Area, CA and requires in-person presence 5 days a week to support physical operations.

In this role you will:

  • Manage the onsite build-out day to day, coordinating daily activities with ongoing construction, contractors, and internal stakeholders

  • Stand up site operating rhythms (daily readiness checks, shift/startup routines, issue triage, and escalation paths) to ensure stable operations during ramp and steady state

  • Own daily site readiness and execution across manufacturing lines, work areas, and warehouse/stockroom spaces

  • Coordinate closely with factory floor operations to align on priorities, line needs, staffing readiness, and execution plans

  • Partner with and coordinate contractor workforces on-site (tasking, standards, safety expectations, performance follow-up, and escalation)

  • Own internal material movement and transport inside the facility (staging runs, line-side replenishment, internal transfers), ensuring flow and safety

  • Maintain clear standards for storage, labeling, staging lanes, workspace organization, and visual controls (5S or similar)

  • Coordinate day-to-day facility operations: access, work orders, basic maintenance scheduling, supply replenishment, space planning, and issue triage/escalation

  • Track and resolve operational issues that affect uptime or flow; drive root cause resolution across Facilities, Safety, Engineering, and Ops

  • Build and maintain SOPs for site operations workflows; train team members/contractors on standard work and safety expectations

  • Partner with Safety, Facilities, Engineering, and Ops teams to maintain a safe, compliant, and reliable operating environment

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have experience standing up and running day-to-day operations in a factory, lab, warehouse, or production-like facility

  • Are highly organized and proactive about keeping environments clean, safe, and execution-ready

  • Can coordinate multiple workflows (build-out, lines, warehousing, internal movement, facilities needs) without losing detail

  • Communicate clearly with frontline teams, contractors, and cross-functional partners and follow through on issues

  • Like improving systems and standard work, not just reacting to problems

  • Are comfortable operating with urgency during ramp while building durable processes for long-term stability

  • Remain calm under pressure, make decisions amid ambiguity, and stay focused on execution

  • Enjoy taking messy, early-stage systems and turning them into reliable, scalable operations

What success looks like:

  • Engineering and floor operations are never blocked by missing parts or emergency maintenance

  • Inventory visibility is high — teams know what is on hand, what is coming, and where it is

  • The site runs on clear processes rather than heroics

  • Contractor operations run smoothly and scale effectively

descriptionHtml:
About the Team
Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and advancing toward AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world environments. Working across the full model and systems stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. About the Role
As a Supply Chain Manager, Material & Partner Management on the Robotics team, you will own the operational and business relationships that enable our manufacturing partners and critical suppliers to execute reliably across development builds and production ramps. You will serve as the primary interface to partners, guiding capacity planning, materials readiness, and delivery commitments to ensure builds can happen on schedule.

You will drive partner operating cadences (build readiness reviews, materials checks, cost and capacity management, QBRs), review schedules and material receiving ladders to provide clear confidence levels on timely and capable execution, and drives escalations as needed for build blockers like shortages, late parts, and quality issues. You will also own the commercial side of partner management, including SOW development, contracts, and ongoing oversight of partner commitments, payments, and performance.


This role is based in San Francisco, and requires in-person presence 5 days a week to support physical operations.

In this role, you will:

Partner Management & Operating Cadence

  • Own end-to-end relationships with key manufacturing partners (CM/JDM/ODM) and critical suppliers, spanning executive alignment through regular operational execution

  • Run joint business operation cadences: planning and capacity reviews, materials readiness checks, and QBRs, with clear owners, actions, and follow-through

  • Serve as the business partner interface across Engineering, Quality, and Technical Ops to keep execution aligned and unblocked

Build Planning & Material Readiness

  • Drive build planning and materials readiness with partners by confirming capacity, long-lead coverage, promise dates, and readiness gates for program ramp

  • Own partner-side material pipelining and readiness visibility, surfacing risks early and driving mitigation plans

Performance Management, Escalations, and Issue Resolution

  • Manage partner performance using scorecards and readiness metrics (delivery, quality, responsiveness, readiness health) and lead corrective actions when performance falls below bar

  • Lead cross-functional escalation and issue resolution for build blockers (shortages, late parts, quality escapes), coordinating Engineering, Quality, and Technical Ops

  • Drive durable closure on recurring issues by tightening processes, owners, and partner accountability mechanisms

  • Build continuous improvement programs with partners to increase yield, reliability, documentation quality, and repeatable processes

Commercial Ownership: SOWs, Contracts, and Business Operations

  • Own the business relationship with major partners, including commercial alignment and ongoing operational management

  • Develop Statements of Work (SOWs) and drive contract development and review in partnership with Legal
    Oversee partner business operations such as contracts, payments, and commercial commitments, ensuring alignment to build execution and materials readiness

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have owned execution with CM/JDM/ODM partners and can drive materials readiness against build plans and ramps

  • Are great at running partner cadences (readiness reviews, issue triage, QBRs) with clear owners and follow-through

  • Can assess build schedules + receiving ladders, make a confident on-time call, and close gaps fast

  • Lead escalations for shortages, late parts, and quality issues while coordinating Engineering, Quality, and Tech Ops end-to-end

  • Can manage the commercial side: SOWs, contract coordination with Legal, and ongoing partner business operations

  • Understand complex BOMs and fast hardware development cycles, ideally with final assembly

  • Enjoy owning large partner relationships and operating as the single point of accountability for successful collaboration

You will also own the commercial side of partner management, including SOW development, contracts, and ongoing oversight of partner commitments, payments, and performance.


This role is based in San Francisco, and requires in-person presence 5 days a week to support physical operations.


In this role, you will:

Partner Management & Operating Cadence

 - Own end-to-end relationships with key manufacturing partners (CM/JDM/ODM) and critical suppliers, spanning executive alignment through regular operational execution

 - Run joint business operation cadences: planning and capacity reviews, materials readiness checks, and QBRs, with clear owners, actions, and follow-through

 - Serve as the business partner interface across Engineering, Quality, and Technical Ops to keep execution aligned and unblocked

Build Planning & Material Readiness

 - Drive build planning and materials readiness with partners by confirming capacity, long-lead coverage, promise dates, and readiness gates for program ramp

 - Own partner-side material pipelining and readiness visibility, surfacing risks early and driving mitigation plans

Performance Management, Escalations, and Issue Resolution

 - Manage partner performance using scorecards and readiness metrics (delivery, quality, responsiveness, readiness health) and lead corrective actions when performance falls below bar

 - Lead cross-functional escalation and issue resolution for build blockers (shortages, late parts, quality escapes), coordinating Engineering, Quality, and Technical Ops

 - Drive durable closure on recurring issues by tightening processes, owners, and partner accountability mechanisms

 - Build continuous improvement programs with partners to increase yield, reliability, documentation quality, and repeatable processes

Commercial Ownership: SOWs, Contracts, and Business Operations

 - Own the business relationship with major partners, including commercial alignment and ongoing operational management

 - Develop Statements of Work (SOWs) and drive contract development and review in partnership with Legal
   Oversee partner business operations such as contracts, payments, and commercial commitments, ensuring alignment to build execution and materials readiness

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have owned execution with CM/JDM/ODM partners and can drive materials readiness against build plans and ramps

 - Are great at running partner cadences (readiness reviews, issue triage, QBRs) with clear owners and follow-through

 - Can assess build schedules + receiving ladders, make a confident on-time call, and close gaps fast

 - Lead escalations for shortages, late parts, and quality issues while coordinating Engineering, Quality, and Tech Ops end-to-end

 - Can manage the commercial side: SOWs, contract coordination with Legal, and ongoing partner business operations

 - Understand complex BOMs and fast hardware development cycles, ideally with final assembly

title: Buyer
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and pushing towards AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world settings. Working across the entire model stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the constraints of physical systems to improve peoples’ lives.

About the Role

We’re seeking a Buyer to support vendor execution and purchase order delivery for finished goods. In this role, you will manage day-to-day vendor interactions, drive purchase orders through procurement and finance processes, and support delivery tracking through handoff to logistics partners. You will work closely with engineering, operations, procurement, and finance teams to ensure purchasing decisions are executed accurately and on time, escalating risks and issues as needed.

This role sits at the execution layer of procurement. Sourcing strategy, supplier selection, and technical specifications are defined by internal stakeholders. This role ensures those decisions are translated into clean purchase orders, reliable vendor execution, and predictable delivery.

This role is based in the San Francisco Bay Area and requires in-person work five days per week.

In this role, you will:

  • Support and manage relationships with assigned vendors supplying finished goods.

  • Request, validate, and confirm vendor quotes based on defined commercial and technical requirements.

  • Ensure incoterms, delivery responsibilities, and handoff points are clearly documented and aligned with vendors.

  • Track vendor commitments, promise dates, and delivery status.

  • Create purchase orders and drive them through procurement, legal, and finance approval workflows.

  • Ensure purchase orders reflect accurate commercial and delivery terms, including pricing, quantities, ship-to locations, incoterms, promise dates, and payment terms.

  • Release purchase orders to vendors and confirm acknowledgements and delivery schedules.

  • Process purchase order changes related to quantity, timing, scope, or delivery terms as requirements evolve.

  • Monitor delivery timelines, flag risks or delays, and engage vendors to clarify changes or issues.

  • Escalate delivery, timing, or execution risks as needed and support issue resolution.

  • Partner with engineering, operations, and planning teams to align demand and timing.

  • Hand off approved purchase orders and vendor details to logistics coordinators for shipment execution.

  • Maintain clear communication with stakeholders on status, risks, and changes.

  • Ensure procurement and finance systems reflect accurate, up-to-date purchasing data.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have experience executing purchase orders and coordinating with external vendors.

  • Understand incoterms and how they affect delivery responsibilities, risk transfer, and timing.

  • Are comfortable navigating procurement, legal, and finance approval workflows.

  • Can manage multiple open orders and vendor commitments with strong attention to detail.

  • Communicate clearly across engineering, operations, procurement, and finance teams.

  • Follow established processes while escalating risks and issues with good judgment.

Nice to have:

  • Experience in hardware, manufacturing, robotics, or technical operations environments.

  • Exposure to international suppliers, cross-border shipments, or complex delivery environments.

  • Experience working in ERP or procurement systems.

title: Technical Revenue Lead
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI Finance helps ensure the organization is set up for success in pursuit of its mission of ensuring that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity.

Within Finance, the Revenue Assurance and Strategy team partners with Product, Growth, Legal, Deal Desk, GTM, and Revenue Accounting to support scalable, audit-ready monetization. We focus on:

  • Revenue Strategy: advising on product and pricing design, monetization models, and contract structuring to enable growth while aligning with ASC 606

  • Revenue Assurance: ensuring revenue recognition conclusions are technically sound, consistently operationalized, and supported by documentation, controls, and system readiness

We evaluate revenue impacts of self-serve monetization models, complex enterprise contracts, and evolving offerings, and we work closely with systems and engineering partners to drive automation.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Technical Revenue Leader to own product and monetization advisory, support revenue recognition across our professional services portfolio, and drive scalable frameworks for revenue accounting as OpenAI’s products and commercial motions evolve.

Reporting to the Head of Technical Revenue, you will serve as a trusted advisor in high-ambiguity spaces where product design, pricing, contracting, and accounting intersect. You will help define the accounting posture and operational approach for new and changing revenue streams, and partner across teams to ensure we maintain strong controllership standards as we scale.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Serve as the primary revenue advisor for new product launches, pricing changes, and evolving monetization models, establishing scalable ASC 606 positions where precedent does not yet exist.

  • Translate technical conclusions into practical guardrails that influence product design, deal structure, and go-to-market strategy.

  • Partner closely with Growth, GTM, StratFin, Legal, and Deal Desk to proactively embed revenue considerations into contract negotiations and product development.

  • Draft and maintain technical accounting memos and policies to document positions on complex arrangements under ASC 606.

  • Collaborate with Finance Systems and Engineering teams to drive automation initiatives for contract intake, SSP allocation, and revenue reporting.

  • Define long-term priorities for revenue automation and improvements to processes and controls.

  • Mentor and guide the technical revenue team, elevating the team’s ability to proactively influence product and contract decisions.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • 10+ years of technical revenue accounting experience, with strong expertise in ASC 606 across SaaS, consumption-based, and professional services arrangements.

  • Proven experience advising Product and GTM teams on pricing, monetization strategy, and revenue recognition implications — influencing deal and product design before launch.

  • Demonstrated ability to bridge technical accounting conclusions with system implementation, ensuring revenue treatment is both GAAP-compliant and operationally scalable.

  • Experience navigating emerging monetization models such as advertising revenue, hardware-enabled offerings, marketplaces/commerce platforms, or other multi-sided ecosystems is a strong plus.

  • Deep contract review experience, including multi-element arrangements, milestone-based SOWs, credit/usage models, and complex enterprise agreements.

  • Familiarity with order-to-cash workflows and revenue automation tools (e.g., Oracle Fusion, NetSuite ARM, RevPro, Salesforce CPQ), with a systems mindset toward scale.

  • Strong executive communication skills, with the ability to translate complex accounting guidance into clear, actionable advice for non-accounting stakeholders.

  • CPA strongly preferred; a mix of Big 4 (or accounting advisory) and tech industry experience in high-growth environments is highly valued.
